clue.text: He will not save himself

parts.note: reads like a man refusing to rescue himself, but means someone who never puts money by

explanation.surface: A man refuses to rescue himself from danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel squanders money and saves none of it for himself.

clue.text: Solid pair is married

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married in records and lists

explanation.surface: A couple who are solid together are married.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a prism is a solid figure with matching polygonal ends.

clue.text: Scrooge pulling up but not stopping

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the remaining letters are read bottom to top
a word that does not stop loses its final letter, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: pulling means dragging

explanation.surface: Ebenezer Scrooge hauls something upwards without a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not stopping' cuts the final G from DRAGGING to leave DRAGGIN, and 'up' turns that round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge, from Dickens, is the byword for a miser, and a stingy hoarder is a skinflint.

clue.text: One caught in 21 gives angry outburst

indicators.note: one piece is caught inside another, so the letter goes within the word for 21

parts.note: the answer to 21 down is traffic, which means trade
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a traffic jam lets fly with a furious rant.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 21 down, whose definition 'Trade' supplies the letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: A rant or harangue is a long angry speech of denunciation.

clue.text: Went to haunt Edward

parts.note: a haunt is a favourite place, a resort
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone went off to haunt a man called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haunt' looks like a ghostly verb but is the noun for a place often visited.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resorted to a place or remedy is to have gone or turned to it.

clue.text: Anatole with society girl

parts.note: Anatole France was a French novelist, so the first name stands for his surname

explanation.surface: Anatole goes out with a society girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatole France won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1921.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Too self-assured on high to reveal set of books

parts.note: on high means above, over
to confide is to reveal a secret
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A cocky person up high is about to reveal a shelf of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocky people are excessively certain of their own abilities.

clue.text: Parsley's unusually thinly scattered

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone's parsley has been sprinkled very sparingly over a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread out with wide gaps, in a meagre or scanty way.

clue.text: The biggest wave so far?

parts.note: reads as a question about surfing or the sea, but means anything that beats the best ever achieved

explanation.surface: A surfer wonders whether this is the largest wave ever ridden.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that outdoes every previous best sets a new best mark.

clue.text: Trying to do better than violet, say, with gin sling

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the short name sounds when spoken

parts.note: Vi is the short form of the girl's name Violet

indicators.note: to sling is to toss about, so these three letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to outdo a violet cocktail by mixing a gin sling.
explanation.walkthrough: Vi, short for Violet, is pronounced 'vye', written VY; 'sling' rearranges GIN to ING. A gin sling is also a cocktail, which is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete, so competing means striving to outdo a rival.

clue.text: Got up to the fruit of a tree in eastern India

definitions.text: Got up to the fruit of a tree in eastern India

parts.note: got up means rose, as from bed
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone climbed up to pick the fruit of an Indian tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree of the East Indies bears this rose-scented fruit, also called jambu.

clue.text: He has a smashing time shopping

definitions.text: He has a smashing time shopping

parts.words: He has a smashing time shopping
parts.note: sounds like a happy shopper, but describes a thief who drives a vehicle through a shop window

explanation.surface: A man enjoys a wonderful day out at the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal who crashes a car into a store front to loot it.

clue.text: Load vehicle with energy

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Someone loads a vehicle with energy supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight or goods carried by a ship or plane is its load.

clue.text: One accepted Sidney being in position to strike the ball

definitions.text: in position to strike the ball

indicators.note: one word accepts another, taking it inside itself

parts.note: taken as written
Sid is the short form of the name Sidney

explanation.surface: Someone welcomed Sidney, who was ready to hit the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby, a player level with or behind the ball may legally play it; 'accepted' places the short name inside after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Not offside, so a player is legally placed to play the ball.

clue.text: Reportedly made a mistake going to capital with combined symptoms

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is to be taken as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: made a mistake means sinned, erred
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Someone apparently erred in travelling to a capital while showing a cluster of symptoms.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for a set of signs that occur together and mark a condition.

clue.text: Support for those who are retired

definitions.text: Support for those who are retired

parts.words: Support for those who are retired
parts.note: sounds like a pension or care for the elderly, but retired here means gone to bed

explanation.surface: A scheme offering help to pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: The frame that holds a mattress supports sleepers who have turned in for the night.

clue.text: Pilot, he's manoeuvring at landing-place

indicators.note: manoeuvring suggests moving the letters about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pilot is manoeuvring his aircraft at the landing site.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pad where helicopters touch down.

clue.text: Completed fiendish arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters means putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has completed a devilishly clever plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Done, ended, brought to a close.

clue.text: Stop being stout and firm

definitions.meaning: to stem a flow, as of blood from a wound
loyal and steadfast, or strong and solidly built

explanation.surface: Someone stops being sturdy and resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: One word both means to stem a flow and describes a loyal, steadfast supporter.

clue.text: Not a drop-out in the long run

definitions.text: Not a drop-out in the long run

parts.words: Not a drop-out in the long run
parts.note: sounds like someone who completes a course eventually, but means a runner or horse with endurance over distance

explanation.surface: Someone who ultimately does not give up their studies.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or athlete with stamina, good over long distances.

clue.text: Trade — on this island?

definitions.meaning: commerce, dealing in goods, often illicit
a ... island is the raised refuge in the middle of a road

explanation.surface: A trader wonders whether business happens on this island.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means dealing in goods, and it names the road island where pedestrians wait.

clue.text: More derogatory bos'n I derided somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sailor admits to mocking the boatswain rather nastily.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective for sneering, mean-spirited remarks.

clue.text: Skin turning red turned back after midnight

indicators.note: turning means the colour word is read backwards
turned back means the time abbreviation is also written backwards

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, covers the hours just after midnight

explanation.surface: Skin went red and then pale again in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' gives DER from RED, and 'turned back' gives MA from AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The dermis, the layer of skin beneath the surface.

clue.text: It is mainly between southern Italy, Sicily and Greece

definitions.text: It is mainly between southern Italy, Sicily and Greece

parts.words: It is mainly between southern Italy, Sicily and Greece
parts.note: reads as a vague geography fact with mainly meaning chiefly, but mainly also hints at the main, the sea

explanation.surface: A geography lesson locating something in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: This arm of the Mediterranean lies off western Greece and south of Italy's heel.

clue.text: Ointment takes up most of the tray

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a salver is a flat serving tray

explanation.surface: A jar of ointment takes up nearly all the space on the tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing balm applied to wounds or sore skin.

clue.text: Proposed maiden, not eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone proposed to a girl, who was not at all odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Put forward as a candidate for election or an award.

clue.text: Wrong river to the south-east

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, England
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: Someone went the wrong way down a river towards the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a Cornish river that flows out at Falmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect, untrue.

clue.text: Mainly ruined

parts.note: looks like largely destroyed, but the main is the sea, so it means wrecked at sea

explanation.surface: Something is for the most part spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranded or lost after a vessel founders at sea.
